question: Who owns an upload after a placeholder moves, disappears, is undone or outlives its editor, and can provider-specific state be removed?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest pursue verdict, at queue position 19. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: One user gesture follows one law. An external file drop lands where the indicator shows, through the same landing rules as a block drag, and a refused drop inserts nothing (DnD consolidation plan, media and dnd docs).
Every public configuration key represents a distinct user job, because names, flags and config keys are public API (VISION.md, docs/vision/plate.md).

Upload validates and inserts a batch atomically, starts transfer after commit, keeps files, authority, progress and failures local to each live NodeKey, and completes into the installed media schema type (docs/vision/plate.md 379-393).
Removal, retagging, plugin cleanup and whole-document replacement revoke requests; history never restarts them.
Provider, gateway, storage and durable URL policy stay in copied application recipes; Plate exposes only the single-file UploadClient with Files SDK types.
Public docs describe the current behavior only.
evidenceReuse: Reused the uploads decision page, the 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-21 reviews and outcomes (draft slot, Files SDK client, provider items, browser naming) and the 2026-10-01 DnD consolidation plan and executions. Rechecked on the live tree: BaseUploadPlugin admission, task lifetime, completion and insertData interceptor; the React UploadPlugin drop handlers and spec; Plite's applyEditableDragOver and applyEditableDrop fallthrough; the copied upload.tsx kit, upload/browser.ts and registry features; the media, dnd and upload docs; Plite plugin cleanup reasons; and the absence of any DnD file handling in dnd.tsx. No uncommitted changes touch these files.
summary: The job is to admit files, keep draft identity and request authority through moves, removal, undo and document replacement, complete into the installed media schema, and keep provider state in copied recipes. Live source holds that. BaseUploadPlugin keys tasks by NodeKey and admitting view, cancels on slot loss, retagging, the documentReplacement annotation and plugin cleanup, vetoes cross-root draft moves, completes through the installed media descriptor, and depends only on Files SDK call and outcome types. upload-browser, createBrowserUploadKit and upload/browser.ts replace every ephemeral name, and no runtime provider switch remains. The new gap comes from the DnD consolidation. nativeDrop defaulted to false so the React adapter would defer to DnD's file routing (the spec still says it leaves drops to the DnD owner), but DnD no longer handles files. An app without the copied kit therefore gets file drops placed after the drop caret's block by the insertData interceptor, with no drop indicator, no landing rules and an html-wins rule the drop handler does not share. The strongest alternatives are deleting nativeDrop so the React adapter owns every external file drop through resolveDropTarget, or keeping a toggle whose off state truly declines drops. An editor-destruction lifecycle and descriptor imports for media destinations both lose (see alternatives).

callSites.current: Copied kit: UploadPlugin.configure({ component: UploadElement, initialState: { client, getUrl, rules, maxFiles, nativeDrop: true, onError } }). Package default (nativeDrop: false): UploadPlugin's on.drop returns undefined, Plite's applyEditableDrop runs tx.selection.set(range); tx.command(domCommands.insertData, data), and BaseUploadPlugin's insertData interceptor calls tx.upload.submit(files, { after: caretBlockKey, replaceEmpty: true }) with no indicator or landing rules.
callSites.proposed: UploadPlugin.configure({ component, initialState: { client, getUrl, rules, maxFiles, onError } }) with nativeDrop deleted (proposed); UploadPlugin's on.dragOver and on.drop always run editor.api.dom.resolveDropTarget(event, { files }) for Files drags, submit with editor.plugin(BaseUploadPlugin).update.submit(files, { before | after: key }), and consume a refused drop, so the insertData interceptor handles paste only.

alternatives: Keeping the current design (Stop) loses. The rename landed and the lifetime laws hold, but the package default routes drops through the path the DnD design calls policy-less, and the docs and spec describe a DnD owner and an off switch that no longer exist.

Deleting nativeDrop is the proposed lane. The React UploadPlugin resolves every external Files drop with resolveDropTarget, submits at the keyed edge and consumes a refused drop, and the insertData interceptor then serves paste only. That gives one law and one fewer config key, and the docs become true.

Keeping a toggle, defaulting it on and making off consume file drops without uploading is viable only if best-api finds a real opt-out job. It keeps a config key and still needs the html-versus-files rule settled.
Teaching Plite's neutral caret drop to resolve block edges for void-block payloads loses. It changes the Plite drop law for all data to serve one Plate feature.

Adding an editor-destruction lifecycle so uploads cancel when an app discards an editor loses for now. Plite has no editor-destruction signal (cleanup reasons are remove, replace, rollback), doctrine gives apps destruction ownership, and orphaned server objects need gateway cleanup regardless.

Importing the four media descriptors instead of the named getCompiledPlatePlugin lookup and normalizeUrl check loses. The Files SDK design chose optional named destinations so upload does not pull every media plugin, and list, indent and toc use the same private lookup.
proofLimits: Source review only; no unit, browser or provider test was run. The default-configuration drop path is traced through source and has no browser replay (files-sdk.spec.ts drops into the playground kit, which sets nativeDrop true). Whether some app relies on caret-placed file drops is unknown. Live S3, deployed gateways, native devices and performance are outside this review. Editor-discard cancellation is described from source, not measured.
